newsitem.title: INDIA: German defence minister seeks stronger India links.
newsitem.headline: German defence minister seeks stronger India links.

text.p: Germany is keen to strengthen its security ties with India, German defence minister Volker Ruehe said on Wednesday.

"Today we see the opportunity to enlarge the scope of our bilateral cooperation in security affairs...," Ruehe told diplomats and defence experts at a meeting organised by India's state-backed Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses.
Ruehe, who arrived in New Delhi earlier on Wednesday for a three-day visit, stressed India's strategic position in Asia and the united Germany's strengths as a key to wider Indo-German relations.
He said Germany would like security relations to grow beyond mere support in military education and training.

"After the German unification, the end of the East-West conflict and the Indian decision to strengthen its policy of regional and international cooperation, our partnerships can be based on a wider footing," Ruehe said.

Ruehe also took the opportunity to stress the need for countries to sign the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT), describing it as one of the "most important nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament measures concluded to date".
He did not directly mention India, which opposes the treaty as unfair, but said "we strongly appeal to all the states that have not signed the CTBT to do so".
"It is high time to prohibit further nuclear weapon test explosions once and for all," he said.
